src/agent_runtime/observability/init.py

Python · Tier A

Expose request-scoped events, safe sinks and Agent trace types.

Responsibilities

  • Re-export the event, context, redaction, formatting and trace interfaces used by API/runtime callers.

Boundaries

  • This facade provides no execution controller, authorization decision or completion proof.

Lifecycle

  • Consumers construct request contexts and sinks after imports; no trace store is instantiated here.

State

  • Only exported class/function bindings are created; trace persistence remains opt-in at the store.

Security

  • Use ObservabilityContext for sanitized fan-out; constructing an event alone does not redact its values.

Collaborators

  • context.py controls emission; agent_trace.py stores traces; sinks.py chooses output destinations.

Public surface

  • all preserves the established event constants, context factories, trace classes and sink API.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/23-observability.md

@see src/agent_runtime/observability/context.py

src/agent_runtime/observability/activity_page.py

Python · Tier A

Turn retained trace windows into readable Activity pages without hydrating full traces. activity_page obtains cursor context and timing; project_page applies shared redaction, optional cumulative-progress grouping and byte-aware preview compaction. Command identity and inspector links survive shortened detail. Exact mode preserves event selection, not unbounded payload text. These helpers read retained state and never execute commands or alter permission.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
activity_page 136 Read one retained history window and its needed command-start context, timing and generation. A changed generation restarts at the latest page; a missing request returns None. Shared projection_scope captures redaction policy for this read without fetching a full trace or executing work.
project_page 170 Build bounded activity previews and inspector links from a supplied window. Compact mode coalesces only explicitly cumulative progress and separates command output for on-demand inspection; exact mode disables that grouping but still projects/redacts and shortens previews. Preserve lifecycle identity and context ahead of large diagnostics, and base cursors on raw scanned events so hidden/grouped rows do not break paging.

src/agent_runtime/observability/agent_trace.py

Python · Tier A

Maintain request traces, activity details and timing views for the Agent UI.

Responsibilities

  • Collect sanitized events, synchronize SSE readers, track request presentation state and project timing/usage metrics.

Boundaries

  • Traces describe execution owned by the native runtime; they do not resume work or authorize mutations.

Lifecycle

  • Create or restore a request, append events through lifecycle transitions, serve snapshots and evict old requests.

State

  • RLock/Condition protect bounded request/detail maps; optional TraceJournal persists selected requests; raw payloads stay separately keyed.

Security

  • Event fields are redacted before retention; activity storage accepts only public detail models and enforces count/byte bounds.

Collaborators

  • context.py feeds AgentTraceSink; trace_journal.py persists selected traces; tool_activity.py supplies safe inspector sections.

Public surface

  • AgentTraceStore owns snapshots/events/status/timing; AgentTraceSink converts pipeline events; trace models preserve API shape.

@see src/agent_runtime/observability/context.py

src/agent_runtime/observability/async_notifications.py

Python · Tier A

Wake asynchronous observers from existing synchronous state writers without allocating polling threads. AsyncNotifications pairs each reader with an asyncio event and requires the caller’s shared writer lock for readiness/registration ordering. One monotonic deadline bounds each wait, and finally removes listeners on success, timeout, cancellation or failure. AgentTraceStore and AgentUiUpdateBroker consume this primitive; it stores no user-facing notification records and performs no delivery.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
AsyncNotifications 20 Fan out writer notifications to cancellable asyncio readers without worker threads or polling. The caller owns the shared writer lock and readiness predicate; this is an observer wakeup primitive, not the user-facing notification inbox.
AsyncNotifications.notify 28 Schedule each registered event on its owning loop. Call while holding the writer lock shared with wait; a closing loop is ignored, and the awakened reader must recheck canonical state.
AsyncNotifications.wait 39 Register under the writer lock, clear the event and recheck readiness under that same lock, then await a wakeup until one monotonic deadline. Return true on readiness or false on timeout. Cancellation and predicate failures propagate after finally removes the listener; spurious notifications do not extend the deadline.

src/agent_runtime/observability/capability_presentation.py

Python · Tier A

Project capability activity labels without conferring execution authority.

Responsibilities

  • Select built-in or registered presentation metadata, generate compact safe context and emit invocation events.

Boundaries

  • Labels and icons cannot classify execution safety or prove a result; effect and status facts come from callers.

Lifecycle

  • Capability execution requests a started/completed/failed presentation; observers receive bounded public metadata.

State

  • Keeps an in-process built-in label table and returns projections; optional event emission uses request context.

Security

  • Select permitted fields instead of serializing arguments, SQL, Gmail bodies or profiles; redact secrets before truncation.

Collaborators

  • operation_preview.py bounds strings and targets; capability registry supplies custom metadata; context.py emits events.

Public surface

  • CapabilityPresentation, safe_operation_presentation and invocation_event support shared desktop/mobile activity labels.

src/agent_runtime/observability/completion_report.py

Python · Tier A

Provide deterministic user-visible receipts when a terminal task lacks an appropriate agent answer. record tracks the delivery policy and resumption epoch in response_metrics and calls the display-message writer with a stable identity. It honors explicit silence, normal answers and waiting states, preserves uncertainty, and does not backfill historical requests or call a model. The caller owns persistence with the terminal event.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
record 25 Reduce request lifecycle events into a retained completion-delivery receipt and publish factual fallback copy through put. Respect explicit silence and existing agent/direct answers; waits and historical traces without a receipt receive no invented recap. Resumption advances a settled epoch, giving repeated terminal delivery the same message identity. A claim that no commands were sent requires explicit preflight nonexecution and known-effect facts; other outcomes remain qualified. No model call or tool content is used.

src/agent_runtime/observability/content_policy.py

Python · Tier A

Exclude device, browser and provider payloads from diagnostics and portable history.

Responsibilities

Identify sensitive-content tool invocations and select non-content receipt metadata.

Boundaries

This is data minimization, not credential detection or optional redaction; exact execution arguments, model tool results and source result storage remain authoritative.

Lifecycle

Applied before diagnostics fan out, including sinks that retain raw events.

State

No secret values are collected; a request-local diagnostic latch lives in its observer.

Security

Transient-content model traces omit free text even when redaction switches are off.

Collaborators

ObservabilityContext owns fanout; activity and handoff consumers use structural.

Public surface

contains_clipboard, structural, diagnostic_event, private_http_diagnostics.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/37-clipboard.md

src/agent_runtime/observability/context.py

Python · Tier A

Gate, sanitize and fan out request-scoped observability events.

Responsibilities

  • Honor enabled/debug policy, apply event redaction and isolate each sink failure; pair stage timing with the profiler.

Boundaries

  • Observability cannot approve operations or change the native task outcome; profiler lifecycle is a separate collaborator.

Lifecycle

  • Build one context from request options, emit stage events during processing and reuse it through runtime context.

State

  • Keeps request ID, sink list, policy and optional profiler in memory; sinks decide external output.

Security

  • Debug-only events require debug mode; emission sanitizes details before callbacks or logs receive them.

Collaborators

  • redaction.py controls event projection; sinks.py provides adapters; profiling.py records stage durations.

Public surface

  • ObservabilityContext, build_observability_context and observability_from_context connect emitters to configured sinks.

@see src/manual/content/architecture/23-observability.md

@see src/agent_runtime/observability/sinks.py

src/agent_runtime/observability/conversation_delivery.py

Python · Tier A

Preserve explicitly published chat fields when private tool diagnostics are reduced to metadata. conversation_event starts with content_policy.diagnostic_event, restores only allowlisted scalar fields for user/assistant messages, progress and marked answer streams, and retains explicit final_response text. It returns a copied event for trace or sink delivery; surrounding projection applies credential policy. Tool bodies, raw provider output and arbitrary event prose cannot become chat through this helper.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

src/agent_runtime/observability/conversation_history.py

Python · Tier A

Recover missing historical clarification and steering messages for display from accepted native receipts, journal exchanges and amendments. The helper uses the registered RAM owner or an existing read-only SQLite file, matches waits to actual ask_user receipts and labels inferred timestamps. It returns an enriched copy only when needed, skips private diagnostic traces and tolerates unavailable legacy SQL data. It neither updates the journal nor resumes a run.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

Prefer the registered RAM owner; otherwise open an existing SQLite file read- only and tolerate older/missing schema or malformed JSON. Skip private-content traces, deduplicate stable message IDs and return a copied payload only when additions exist; native state and original events remain unchanged.

src/agent_runtime/observability/display_messages.py

Python · Tier A

Maintain durable display messages independently of model acceptance and execution state. record consumes explicitly published message/stream events under the trace writer lock, increments revisions, deduplicates sequence fragments and preserves interrupted drafts when a later answer supersedes them. It attaches detached changes to the event and stores the current projection in response_metrics before persistence/broadcast. Completion-report publication shares this writer; arbitrary tool text and forged display revisions are not accepted.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
DisplayMessage 23 Describe retained user-visible prose with a stable identity, monotonically revised content/state, first-publication time and source event. Sequence deduplicates streamed fragments; superseded_by preserves the earlier record while identifying its promoted answer. These presentation fields confer no execution authority.
record 36 Update the persisted header and attach changed messages to this event. Called under the trace writer lock, after sanitization and before journal commit/broadcast. Revisions let live clients merge snapshots without rollback.

src/agent_runtime/observability/events.py

Python · Tier A

Define the structured pipeline event envelope and lifecycle names.

Responsibilities

  • Provide request correlation, timestamps, stage/type, severity, user-facing title and structured details.

Boundaries

  • An event describes reported activity; it does not itself establish execution truth or sanitize payloads.

Lifecycle

  • Emitters construct PipelineEvent values; ObservabilityContext applies visibility and redaction before delivery.

State

  • Each model receives a fresh event ID and UTC timestamp; this module owns no journal or sink.

Security

  • safe_for_user/debug_only are metadata, not permission grants; producers must avoid unsafe titles and summaries.

Collaborators

  • core/ids.py supplies event IDs; context.py and sinks.py consume these models.

Public surface

  • PipelineEvent and the STAGE_/EVENT_STAGE_ constants define shared lifecycle vocabulary.

Symbol Line Documentation

src/agent_runtime/observability/execution_activity.py

Python · Tier A

Supply compact operation context and current thinking/wait labels for refresh without restoring full trace bodies. Helpers prefer current in-memory traces and use narrow journal lookups after eviction. They join command starts, invocation/file context and transfer/output timestamps, project redaction before shortening, and distinguish actual terminal evidence from detached or unresolved work. Parsing a command for named files never executes it or proves a filesystem effect.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
execution_phase 54 Read the newest model/tool boundary from the live trace or narrow journal projection. Distinguish Controller admission wait, model wait and preparation/decision thinking; cancelled admission and tool/terminal boundaries return no thinking label. Never fetch a provider response body or infer completion from silence.
command_contexts 116 Find the latest command-start context for each requested operation, including starts outside the current history page. Live trace presence is authoritative; use journal lookups only after eviction, then apply normal trace projection before returning command strings.
retained_activity 161 Join only the named operation latest invocation, command, transfer and nonempty-output facts into a compact refresh context. Project before shortening, recover older public file context when available, and expose command inspector links and output timestamps without transcripts. Running/detached/unknown completion receipts do not produce a completed_at claim; file names parsed from commands remain intent, not observed filesystem effects.

src/agent_runtime/observability/execution_context.py

Python · Tier A

Extract bounded file context from already-public tool evidence. file_context distinguishes requested paths, observed results, revision-backed writes, transfers and collected artifacts; shell_files conservatively labels static paths named in understood commands. Both omit file contents and retain at most 20 entries, with truncation metadata where available. Upstream projection owns credential filtering; this module never opens paths, evaluates shell expressions or changes execution state.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
file_context 17 Project bounded paths, roles and observed/requested states from already-public tool arguments, result sections and metadata. Prefer resolved result paths and successful revision evidence, include reported transfer/artifact paths, and keep at most 20 unique entries. No file body is copied or path opened; the caller is responsible for input projection.
shell_files 120 Parse only bounded, statically understood shell syntax for named input/output/source/destination paths. Ignore opaque syntax and unsupported commands, never evaluate dynamic expressions, and return at most 20 entries marked Named in command without claiming those files exist.

src/agent_runtime/observability/latency.py

Python · Tier A

Attribute local inference work without changing execution or authority.

Responsibilities

Produce bounded typed call timelines and null-safe overlap views.

Boundaries

No inference, authorization, context selection, retry or cancellation policy.

Lifecycle

Capture an existing decision/call, observe owner transitions, publish once.

State

ContextVar propagates to owned workers; offsets share only PROCESS_EPOCH. Records have at most 96 spans; trace views retain at most 64 calls per request.

Security

No prompts, tool results, credentials or endpoint query strings are retained.

Collaborators

tracing supplies call IDs and storage; native projection and transport owners supply observations; agent_trace projects the existing activity stream.

Public surface

decision/traced_call bind capture; measured/span/mark observe work; records_from_events and aggregate build explicit inspection views, never execution state. Provider durations have no local position and are never added to transport elapsed time.

src/agent_runtime/observability/memory_model_output.py

Python · Tier A

Store diagnostic provider output in immutable RAM pages under the controller state hub, with standalone memory mode for fixtures. Checkpoint adapters load/write SQL representations; request tombstones, retention transactions and process-local notifications protect late publication and reader isolation.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

src/agent_runtime/observability/memory_trace_journal.py

Python · Tier A

Own live trace headers, immutable event pages, lookup indexes, deletion tombstones and the event sequence in the Controller state hub. Recovery/checkpoint callbacks translate the SQLite representation; runtime methods reject direct SQL and return detached projections. AgentTraceStore supplies already-projected events and coordinates IDs, while retention hooks join writes in the same transaction. Paging and restoration do not authorize execution or reconstruct missing receipts.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

Explicit expiry removes only recognized timeline diagnostics; business events are not subject to that retirement request.

Reject mismatched payload identities, normalize duplicate capabilities and recover a sequence beyond every stored ID, including orphan events. Restore tombstones so delayed writes cannot resurrect deleted requests.
